title: VPN clients unable to establish tunnel after maintenance window
reported_symptom: Remote employees report they cannot connect to the corporate VPN; the client hangs at 'Negotiating security policies' and eventually times out.
error_details: IKE_SA phase 2 failed: NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN; strongSwan charon: received AUTHENTICATION_FAILED notify error; retransmit 5 of request message ID 0
root_cause: A firmware update on the VPN concentrator reset the IKEv2 proposal list, dropping AES-256-GCM which the client profiles required, leaving no matching cipher proposal between peers.
resolution_steps: Compare the pre- and post-maintenance IKEv2 proposal configuration on the concentrator
Re-add the AES-256-GCM / SHA-384 / DH group 20 proposal to the phase 2 policy
Force a re-key and confirm one pilot client establishes a tunnel
Roll out to all client profiles and monitor concentrator SA table

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failures for internal services
reported_symptom: Applications intermittently fail to reach internal hostnames; retries usually succeed a few seconds later.
error_details: dig: ;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached; SERVFAIL for api.internal.corp; resolver returned NXDOMAIN intermittently
root_cause: One of three internal resolvers had a stale root hints file and was silently failing recursive queries; round-robin sent ~1/3 of queries to the bad resolver.
resolution_steps: Query each resolver directly to isolate which returns SERVFAIL
Refresh root hints and flush the cache on the failing resolver
Restart the named service and re-run validation queries
Add a health check to the resolver load-balancer pool

title: Load balancer returning 503 for checkout service
reported_symptom: Customers get an error page at checkout during peak traffic; the site works fine for browsing.
error_details: HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable; HAProxy: backend checkout_be has no server available (all DOWN); health check L7STS/500 in 2001ms
root_cause: The checkout backend health check hit a /healthz endpoint that itself called a slow downstream; under load it exceeded the 2s check timeout, so HAProxy marked all backends down even though they could serve real traffic.
resolution_steps: Confirm backends are actually serving via direct curl to pod IPs
Point the health check at a lightweight /livez endpoint that has no downstream calls
Raise the health-check timeout and increase the rise/fall thresholds
Reload HAProxy and watch the backend UP/DOWN transitions

title: Payment API returning 503 due to upstream connection pool exhaustion
reported_symptom: Payment API sporadically returns errors; error rate climbs with traffic and recovers when traffic drops.
error_details: HTTP/1.1 503; HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms; active=50 idle=0 waiting=37
root_cause: A new reporting job opened long-lived connections without returning them to the pool, starving the payment service which shared the same 50-connection Hikari pool.
resolution_steps: Inspect HikariCP metrics to confirm active connections pinned at max
Identify the reporting job holding connections via pg_stat_activity
Move the reporting workload to a separate pool / read replica
Add a leak-detection threshold and connection max-lifetime

title: Recurring deadlocks on orders table during flash sale
reported_symptom: Order submissions occasionally fail and must be retried by the client during high-traffic sales.
error_details: ERROR: deadlock detected; DETAIL: Process 2841 waits for ShareLock on transaction 99231; Process 2902 waits for ShareLock on transaction 99244; SQLSTATE 40P01
root_cause: Two code paths updated orders and inventory rows in opposite order, so concurrent transactions acquired locks in a cycle under load.
resolution_steps: Capture the deadlock graph from PostgreSQL logs
Standardize lock acquisition order (orders before inventory) across both paths
Add a bounded retry with jitter for SQLSTATE 40P01
Load-test the fix with concurrent order simulation

title: Read replica falling behind primary by several minutes
reported_symptom: Users report seeing stale data on dashboards that read from the replica; writes appear correct on the primary.
error_details: pg_stat_replication: replay_lag = 00:04:37; wal sender state 'catchup'; replica log: recovery still in progress, LSN 3F/A8000000 behind primary
root_cause: A large bulk DELETE on the primary generated a burst of WAL that the single-threaded replay on the replica could not keep up with; disk I/O on the replica saturated.
resolution_steps: Confirm replay_lag trend and check replica disk I/O saturation
Throttle or batch the bulk DELETE on the primary
Increase max_parallel_workers and consider faster storage for the replica
Monitor replay_lag returns to under 5 seconds

title: SSO login loop after IdP metadata rotation
reported_symptom: After signing in, users are bounced back to the login page in an endless redirect loop across all internal apps.
error_details: SAML response validation failed: signature does not match; opensaml: SecurityPolicyException 'Signature trust establishment failed'; HTTP 302 loop between SP and IdP
root_cause: The IdP rotated its signing certificate but the SP's SAML metadata still pinned the old certificate, so every signed assertion failed validation and the SP re-initiated login.
resolution_steps: Reproduce and capture the SAML response with a browser SAML tracer
Fetch and import the IdP's current signing certificate into SP metadata
Reload the SP metadata and clear cached assertions
Verify a full login round-trip succeeds for a test user

title: API calls rejected with 401 after access token expiry not refreshed
reported_symptom: A batch integration starts failing every hour after running fine for the first hour.
error_details: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized; WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="The access token expired"; JWT exp claim in the past
root_cause: The integration cached the OAuth access token but never used the refresh token, so once the 3600s access token expired every request returned 401.
resolution_steps: Decode the failing JWT and confirm the exp claim is in the past
Implement refresh-token exchange before token expiry
Add a 60s early-refresh buffer and retry-on-401 with one re-auth
Verify the integration runs past the token lifetime

title: MFA push notifications not delivered to a subset of users
reported_symptom: Some users never receive the MFA push prompt and are locked out after the timeout; SMS fallback works.
error_details: MFA provider log: APNs response 410 'Unregistered'; FCM error 'NotRegistered'; push token invalidated after device OS upgrade
root_cause: After a mobile OS update, device push tokens were rotated but the MFA app failed to re-register the new token with the provider, so pushes went to dead tokens.
resolution_steps: Correlate affected users to a recent device OS upgrade
Force the MFA app to re-register push tokens on next launch
Purge invalidated tokens (APNs 410 / FCM NotRegistered) from the provider
Confirm push delivery for a re-registered test device

title: Log partition full causing application write failures
reported_symptom: Application suddenly stops accepting requests and the process appears alive but unresponsive.
error_details: OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device; /var/log at 100% (df -h); logrotate: error creating output file: Disk quota exceeded
root_cause: Debug logging was accidentally left enabled in production, filling /var/log; logrotate's compression could not keep pace and the partition hit 100%, blocking all writes including the app's own state files.
resolution_steps: Identify the largest log files with du and confirm partition at 100%
Truncate/compress the runaway debug logs to free space immediately
Revert the log level to WARN in production config
Add a disk-usage alert at 80% and a separate volume for logs

title: Java service OOM killed repeatedly under steady load
reported_symptom: A service restarts every few hours on its own; users see brief error spikes at restart.
error_details: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space; GC overhead limit exceeded; dmesg: Out of memory: Killed process 1892 (java) total-vm:6120484kB
root_cause: An in-memory cache had no eviction policy, so it grew unbounded until the JVM heap was exhausted and the kernel OOM-killer terminated the process.
resolution_steps: Capture a heap dump and confirm the cache dominates retained heap
Add a size/TTL-bounded eviction policy to the cache
Set -Xmx explicitly and enable HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError
Monitor heap usage across a full traffic cycle

title: Kubernetes pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff after config change
reported_symptom: A deployment rolled out and the new pods never become ready; the service is down.
error_details: CrashLoopBackOff; container exited with code 1; kubectl logs: 'FATAL: could not parse config: unexpected key redis_ur'; Back-off restarting failed container
root_cause: A typo in the ConfigMap key (redis_ur instead of redis_url) caused the app to fail config parsing on startup and exit(1), triggering the crash loop.
resolution_steps: Read the crashing container's logs to find the parse error
Fix the ConfigMap key typo (redis_ur -> redis_url)
Roll the deployment to pick up the corrected ConfigMap
Confirm pods reach Ready and add config schema validation to CI

title: Pods evicted due to node memory pressure
reported_symptom: Random pods disappear and reschedule during busy periods; some requests fail during the shuffle.
error_details: Pod evicted: reason 'Evicted' message 'The node was low on resource: memory'; kubelet: attempting to reclaim memory; OOMKilled containers exit code 137
root_cause: Pods had no memory limits set, so a few noisy neighbors consumed node memory until kubelet triggered eviction of lower-priority pods (exit 137).
resolution_steps: Identify the node under memory pressure and the top-consuming pods
Set requests and limits on the offending workloads
Add pod priority classes so critical pods survive eviction
Verify no further evictions during peak load

title: Container image pull failing on new nodes
reported_symptom: Newly scaled nodes cannot start pods; existing pods are fine.
error_details: Failed to pull image: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to pull and unpack image: 401 Unauthorized from registry; ImagePullBackOff
root_cause: The image pull secret expired and was only refreshed on the original node pool; new nodes joined without the valid registry credentials.
resolution_steps: Confirm ImagePullBackOff and the 401 from the registry in pod events
Rotate and re-create the imagePullSecret in the namespace
Patch the service account to reference the new secret
Trigger a new node and confirm images pull successfully

title: Dashboard renders blank on Safari after frontend deploy
reported_symptom: Safari users see a blank white page on the dashboard; Chrome and Firefox work fine.
error_details: Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token '?'; console: optional chaining not supported; bundle used ?. without transpilation target for older Safari
root_cause: A build config change set the Babel target too high, so optional-chaining syntax shipped untranspiled and crashed on older Safari engines.
resolution_steps: Reproduce on the affected Safari version and capture the SyntaxError
Restore the browserslist target to include the supported Safari range
Rebuild and verify the bundle transpiles optional chaining
Add a cross-browser smoke test to the pipeline

title: Client-side API timeouts on reports page
reported_symptom: The reports page spinner runs forever for large date ranges; small ranges load fine.
error_details: AxiosError: timeout of 10000ms exceeded (ECONNABORTED); network tab shows request pending then cancelled; backend responds in ~14s
root_cause: The client's 10s Axios timeout was shorter than the backend's response time for large report queries, so the client aborted a request the server would have completed.
resolution_steps: Confirm the backend completes the query (just slowly) via server logs
Raise the client timeout for the reports endpoint and show progress UI
Add server-side pagination for large date ranges
Verify large-range reports load without client abort

title: Kafka consumer group lag growing without bound
reported_symptom: Downstream data is increasingly stale; events are being produced faster than they are processed.
error_details: consumer lag = 1.2M messages; group coordinator: 'Member rebalance timed out'; error CommitFailedException: 'cannot complete commit since group already rebalanced'
root_cause: A slow message handler exceeded max.poll.interval.ms, causing the consumer to be kicked from the group; the resulting constant rebalancing meant almost no progress was made.
resolution_steps: Confirm growing lag and repeated rebalances in the consumer group
Reduce max.poll.records and move slow work off the poll thread
Increase max.poll.interval.ms to a safe bound
Redeploy and watch lag drain to zero

title: Messages piling up in the dead letter queue
reported_symptom: A monitoring alert fires that the DLQ depth is rising; some customer notifications are not being sent.
error_details: DLQ depth 8,432 and rising; consumer error: 'Deserialization error for partition notifications-3'; SerializationException: unknown magic byte!
root_cause: A producer was upgraded to a new Avro schema without registering it, so consumers using the old schema hit an unknown magic byte and routed every message to the DLQ.
resolution_steps: Sample a DLQ message and confirm the deserialization/magic-byte error
Register the new schema version in the schema registry
Deploy consumers compatible with the new schema
Replay the DLQ back into the main topic and confirm it drains

title: Production deployment failed midway leaving mixed versions
reported_symptom: Users report inconsistent behavior; some requests hit the new version and some the old.
error_details: helm upgrade failed: 'context deadline exceeded'; rollout status: 3 of 8 replicas updated then stalled; readiness probe failing HTTP 500 on new pods
root_cause: The new release required a DB migration that had not run, so new pods failed their readiness probe and the rollout stalled, leaving old and new pods both serving.
resolution_steps: Confirm the stalled rollout and failing readiness on new pods
Run the pending DB migration as a pre-deploy job
Resume the rollout and confirm all replicas become ready
Add a migration gate to the deploy pipeline

title: Rollback failed because previous image was garbage collected
reported_symptom: A bad release went out and the on-call attempt to roll back failed, extending the outage.
error_details: kubectl rollout undo: 'Failed to pull image tag v2.3.1: manifest unknown'; registry GC removed untagged manifests; ErrImagePull on rollback
root_cause: A registry retention policy garbage-collected the prior image, so the rollback had no image to pull; the deploy pipeline relied on 'latest'-style tags that were overwritten.
resolution_steps: Confirm the rollback fails on manifest unknown for the old tag
Rebuild the previous version from the tagged commit and push it
Deploy the rebuilt image to restore service
Switch to immutable image tags and exclude release images from GC

title: CI pipeline failing intermittently on flaky integration tests
reported_symptom: Developers report the pipeline randomly goes red and passes on re-run, slowing merges.
error_details: Test failed: 'Timed out waiting for element'; exit code 1; container ran out of file descriptors: 'too many open files' (EMFILE)
root_cause: The integration test harness leaked HTTP connections across tests, eventually exhausting file descriptors and causing sporadic timeouts depending on test order.
resolution_steps: Reproduce by running the full suite and watching FD count climb
Close/reuse HTTP clients between tests and raise the ulimit in CI
Add test isolation so ordering does not affect resources
Confirm ten consecutive green pipeline runs

title: Alert storm from a single failing node flooding on-call
reported_symptom: On-call is paged dozens of times in minutes for what appears to be one underlying problem.
error_details: PagerDuty: 143 alerts in 4 minutes; Alertmanager: no inhibition rule matched; 'HostDown' fired alongside 40 dependent 'TargetDown' alerts
root_cause: A single node going down triggered every dependent service's individual alert with no inhibition/grouping rules, burying the real signal in noise.
resolution_steps: Confirm all alerts trace back to one node-down event
Add an Alertmanager inhibition rule so HostDown suppresses dependent TargetDown alerts
Group alerts by node and add a repeat-interval
Test by simulating a node failure in staging

title: False-positive disk alerts from a bind-mounted filesystem
reported_symptom: A disk-usage alert fires nightly but the disk is not actually full when checked.
error_details: Alert 'DiskSpaceLow' filesystem=/proc/... usage=100%; node_exporter reporting pseudo-filesystems; label mountpoint duplicated via bind mount
root_cause: The disk alert did not exclude pseudo/bind-mounted filesystems, so node_exporter reported 100% on read-only pseudo mounts that are always 'full', creating nightly false positives.
resolution_steps: Identify which filesystem the alert matches (a pseudo/bind mount)
Add fstype and mountpoint exclusions to the node_exporter collector
Update the alert query to filter real filesystems only
Confirm the alert no longer fires overnight

title: Unusual login pattern flagged for a service account
reported_symptom: The security team is alerted that a service account is authenticating from unexpected geographies.
error_details: SIEM rule 'ImpossibleTravel': logins from 2 countries within 8 minutes; auth log: successful password auth from 185.220.x.x (Tor exit node); no MFA on account
root_cause: A service account's static password was leaked in a committed config file and was being used from external hosts; the account predated the MFA mandate.
resolution_steps: Confirm the impossible-travel logins and identify the source IPs
Immediately rotate the service-account credential and revoke sessions
Remove the secret from the repo history and move it to the vault
Enforce MFA / mTLS and scope the account's permissions down

title: Public API certificate expired causing TLS failures
reported_symptom: All external clients suddenly fail to call the public API; browsers show a security warning.
error_details: SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired; TLS handshake failed: alert certificate_expired (45); openssl: notAfter=Jul 4 2026 GMT
root_cause: The API's TLS certificate auto-renewal (cert-manager) had been silently failing for weeks due to a broken ACME HTTP-01 challenge, and no one noticed until the cert expired.
resolution_steps: Confirm the expired certificate via openssl and the handshake alert
Issue a new certificate manually to restore service immediately
Fix the ACME HTTP-01 challenge routing so auto-renewal works
Add a certificate-expiry alert at 21 days remaining

title: TLS handshake failures between two internal services
reported_symptom: Service A cannot call Service B after a security hardening change; external traffic is unaffected.
error_details: TLS handshake failed: alert handshake_failure (40); 'no cipher suites in common'; Service B now requires TLS 1.3 only, Service A pinned to TLS 1.2
root_cause: A hardening change disabled TLS 1.2 on Service B, but Service A's client library was pinned to TLS 1.2, so the two could not negotiate a common protocol.
resolution_steps: Capture the handshake_failure and confirm the protocol mismatch
Enable TLS 1.3 in Service A's client (or temporarily re-allow 1.2 on B)
Roll out and confirm mTLS handshakes succeed
Coordinate protocol-deprecation changes across dependent services

title: DNS misconfiguration routing internal traffic to the internet
reported_symptom: Requests to an internal service are unexpectedly slow and occasionally hit a public error page.
error_details: dig internal-api.corp -> returns a public IP (CNAME to a parked domain); resolution path leaked to public resolver 8.8.8.8; no NXDOMAIN as expected
root_cause: A wildcard CNAME in the public zone shadowed the internal record after a split-horizon DNS view was accidentally removed, so internal names resolved to public addresses.
resolution_steps: Trace the resolution path and confirm the public CNAME is returned
Restore the split-horizon internal view for the affected zone
Remove or scope the offending wildcard record
Validate internal names resolve to internal IPs from client subnets

title: Database primary failover did not promote a replica
reported_symptom: The primary database went down and the application stayed down instead of failing over.
error_details: Patroni: 'no promotable member found'; replica in state 'streaming' but lag > maximum_lag_on_failover; leader lock not acquired
root_cause: The only healthy replica exceeded maximum_lag_on_failover at the moment of failure, so Patroni refused to promote it to avoid data loss, leaving the cluster leaderless.
resolution_steps: Confirm the failover was blocked by replica lag exceeding the threshold
Manually promote the least-lagged replica after assessing data loss risk
Repoint the application to the new primary
Tune maximum_lag_on_failover and add a second synchronous replica

title: Token expiry causing 401 storms after clock skew
reported_symptom: A whole fleet of services starts rejecting valid tokens at the same time, then recovers.
error_details: HTTP 401 invalid_token 'token used before issued (iat)'; nbf check failed; server clock drifted +90s from NTP; JWT validation window violated
root_cause: NTP sync failed on the auth server, causing its clock to drift ahead; freshly issued tokens appeared to be 'from the future' to validators and were rejected until clocks realigned.
resolution_steps: Correlate the 401 spike with clock drift on the issuing host
Restart/repair NTP and force a time sync on the auth server
Add a small allowed clock-skew (leeway) to token validation
Monitor NTP offset and alert on drift beyond 1s

title: Memory leak in Node.js API growing across days
reported_symptom: A Node service slows down and must be restarted every few days to stay responsive.
error_details: FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory; process RSS climbing linearly; --max-old-space-size hit
root_cause: An event-emitter listener was added per request but never removed, so listeners and their closures accumulated, leaking memory that GC could not reclaim.
resolution_steps: Take heap snapshots over time and diff retained objects
Find the growing listener count and remove listeners on request end
Deploy the fix and watch RSS flatten
Add a memory-growth alert and periodic snapshot in staging

title: Kafka broker under-replicated partitions after disk failure
reported_symptom: Producers see errors and the cluster reports partitions without full replication.
error_details: UnderReplicatedPartitions = 27; NotEnoughReplicasException; producer error 'NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS' (code 19); broker 3 log dir offline
root_cause: A disk failed on broker 3 taking its log directory offline; partitions led by that broker fell below min.insync.replicas so producers with acks=all were rejected.
resolution_steps: Confirm the offline log dir and under-replicated partitions
Replace the failed disk / move the log dir to a healthy volume
Reassign partitions and let replicas catch up to ISR
Verify UnderReplicatedPartitions returns to zero

title: Canary deployment not shifting traffic
reported_symptom: A canary release was started but 100% of traffic still hits the stable version.
error_details: Argo Rollouts: 'canary weight 20% set but 0% observed'; VirtualService weight not applied; istio-proxy config not synced (CDS push failed)
root_cause: The Istio control plane failed to push the updated route config to the sidecars, so the canary weight was recorded but never enforced at the data plane.
resolution_steps: Confirm the rollout set the weight but the mesh did not apply it
Restart the istiod control-plane pod to force a config push
Verify the VirtualService weights propagate to sidecars
Resume the canary and watch real traffic split

title: Frontend infinite re-render freezing the browser tab
reported_symptom: Opening a specific page makes the browser tab freeze and eventually crash.
error_details: Warning: Maximum update depth exceeded; React error: 'Too many re-renders'; CPU pegged at 100% in the render loop
root_cause: A useEffect updated state on every render without a proper dependency array, creating an infinite render loop that pegged the CPU.
resolution_steps: Reproduce and confirm the maximum-update-depth error
Add the correct dependency array / guard to the offending effect
Verify renders settle and CPU returns to idle
Add a lint rule for exhaustive-deps to catch it in future

title: Connection pool exhaustion on the auth service, not the database
reported_symptom: Login requests hang and time out during peak; the database itself looks healthy.
error_details: HTTP 503; 'Timeout acquiring connection from pool'; HikariPool waiting=61 active=20 max=20; but pg_stat_activity shows only 20 sessions
root_cause: Unlike the payment-service incident, here the pool max (20) was simply undersized for peak login concurrency; the database had plenty of headroom, so the fix was pool sizing, not a leak.
resolution_steps: Confirm the DB is healthy and the bottleneck is the app-side pool
Increase the Hikari maximumPoolSize within the DB's connection budget
Add a queue timeout and backpressure on login
Load-test peak login concurrency to validate the new size

title: Prometheus scrape failures causing gaps in dashboards
reported_symptom: Grafana panels show gaps; some targets appear to have no data for stretches of time.
error_details: Prometheus target DOWN: 'context deadline exceeded'; scrape_duration > scrape_timeout; too many series causing 'sample limit exceeded'
root_cause: A service started exposing a high-cardinality metric (per-request label), so scrapes exceeded the timeout and sample limit and were dropped, creating gaps.
resolution_steps: Identify the target failing scrapes and the high-cardinality metric
Drop or aggregate the offending label via metric_relabel_configs
Raise scrape_timeout modestly if still needed
Confirm the target scrapes reliably and gaps disappear

title: Certificate expiry on internal service breaks a scheduled job
reported_symptom: A nightly data-sync job fails; interactive access to the same service works fine.
error_details: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid; TLS alert certificate_expired (45); the job pinned an internal CA cert that rotated
root_cause: Unlike the public-API cert incident, here the job had pinned a specific internal CA certificate that was rotated on schedule; the job's truststore was never updated, so only that client broke.
resolution_steps: Confirm only the pinned-cert client fails while others succeed
Update the job's truststore with the rotated internal CA
Move from a pinned leaf to trusting the CA chain
Add the truststore update to the CA rotation runbook

title: Load balancer 502 from idle-timeout mismatch with backend
reported_symptom: Users occasionally get an error on long-lived requests; retrying works.
error_details: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway; nginx: 'upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header'; backend keep-alive 60s vs LB idle 75s
root_cause: The backend's keep-alive timeout (60s) was shorter than the load balancer's idle timeout (75s), so the backend closed connections the LB still considered open, producing 502s on reused connections.
resolution_steps: Correlate 502s with connection reuse near the 60s mark
Set the backend keep-alive timeout higher than the LB idle timeout
Reload and confirm the premature-close errors stop
Document the timeout ordering rule (backend > LB idle)

title: Kubernetes job pods OOMKilled with exit 137 during batch run
reported_symptom: A nightly batch Job fails partway; the pod restarts and fails again.
error_details: State: Terminated Reason: OOMKilled exit code 137; container memory limit 512Mi exceeded; last log line mid-batch before kill
root_cause: The batch loaded the entire input file into memory instead of streaming it; larger nightly inputs exceeded the 512Mi container limit and were OOMKilled (exit 137) — same exit code as the eviction incident but a different cause.
resolution_steps: Confirm OOMKilled exit 137 and correlate with input size
Refactor the batch to stream/process the input in chunks
Right-size the container memory limit for the workload
Re-run the nightly Job and confirm it completes

title: Consumer lag alert was a false positive after topic re-partition
reported_symptom: A Kafka lag alert fired but consumers are actually healthy and processing in real time.
error_details: Alert 'ConsumerLagHigh' lag=500k on partitions 6-11; but end-to-end latency normal; lag exporter reading offsets for newly added partitions with no committed offset
root_cause: The topic was expanded from 6 to 12 partitions; the lag exporter treated the new partitions' missing committed offsets as huge lag, a false positive while consumers were fine.
resolution_steps: Confirm real end-to-end latency is normal despite the reported lag
Let consumers commit offsets on the new partitions (or seed them)
Fix the exporter to ignore partitions without committed offsets
Confirm the alert clears and add a guard for future re-partitions

title: SSO outage from expired SAML signing certificate
reported_symptom: No one can log in to any SSO-protected application company-wide.
error_details: SAML: 'The signing certificate is expired'; IdP metadata notAfter passed; SP rejects assertion with 'certificate_expired'; distinct from the earlier metadata-rotation loop
root_cause: Unlike the earlier SSO loop (wrong pinned cert after rotation), here the IdP's signing certificate simply expired with no rotation performed, so every assertion it signed was invalid.
resolution_steps: Confirm the IdP signing certificate is expired (not merely rotated)
Generate and install a new IdP signing certificate
Publish updated IdP metadata and refresh it on all SPs
Add an IdP signing-cert expiry alert at 30 days
